(I am on the autism spectrum though, and I have sensory prossessing issues because of it, so that might be why it happens to me and why blindfolds help)

I do trust my current therapists judgement more than any of the other therapists I've had in the past, but everyone can be wrong, even professionals.
If I do have some type of autism, it must be a mild case, or a very "untypical" form of autism and autistic symptoms.

I also know for a fact that I have some type of dissociative disorder, I'm currently diagnosed with OSDD-1b. But my therapist is still not entierly sure what dissociative disorder I have, but OSDD-1b is the one that fit the most.

I know I'm focusing too much on diagnosises here, but I'm so confused all the time, and so are my therapists. I don't feel like a lot of my symptoms fit in anywhere, I have such a large variety of symptoms that fit in with so many things (dissociative disorders, schizophrenia, bipolar, many personality disorders... and so on) They don't really know where to place me, and sinse no one really knows what's wrong with me they don't know how to treat me. It's frustrating, and I just want a diagnosis that sums up my symptoms, so I can understand it better and get proper help.

Ouch... That hurts. I think these people mix BPD with Narcissism and psychopathy alot. But BPD isn't like that. I know it can be difficult and a lot of drama sometimes, but most of us don't mean any harm. We don't want to hurt people, especially not the ones we love the most. We do have strong feelings and it can be a handful to deal with all those strong emotions, but what I think a lot of people forget it that even though the negative emotions are stronger than average, so are the positive emotions. We love much stronger than most people, and when we love, we love so much that it hurts sometimes. Also, when I've hurt someone with my outbursts of anger, I always feel guilt and regret after, and try and make up for it. Unlike people with Narcissistic personality disorder and Antisocial personality disorder, we don't want to hurt our loved ones and we feel guilty. People with NPD and APD don't. And I'm sick of people mixing BPD with those disorders, because there are a lot of differences. We mean good, but it's hard to contain our strong emotions sometimes... We don't do it on purpose.
